demoCaption: Default replies with sample names and numbers. Your saved messages can differ.
metaDesc: Build a Twitch death counter with ItsBagelBot custom counters. Track a channel total or per-viewer counts, count from chat, and reset between runs.
title: Keep the count through every attempt.
lead: Use a custom counter as your Twitch death counter. Create a channel total called deaths, bump it with a chat command like !death, and reset it for the next run. Counters also support separate values per viewer, per command, or per viewer and command.
howTitle: Create a counter for your next run.
step1Desc: Add a channel counter named deaths on the Counters page. Counters are created, set, reset, renamed and deleted there.
step2Desc: Make a custom command such as !death, turn on its Bump a counter option and pick deaths. Each use adds 1. Channel-point rewards can bump counters too.
step3Desc: A moderator can type !death -1 to undo a miss or !death 5 to add several at once. Reset or set deaths on the Counters page for a fresh attempt.
tblTitle: Chat commands that change the count.
tblNote: Your custom command with Bump a counter turned on does the counting, and its permission decides who can use it. A moderator or the streamer can add a signed number to set the step. Anyone else's number is ignored and the step stays +1.
row2Outcome: Adds 5 to deaths. A plus sign works too: !death +5.
row3Outcome: Removes 1 from deaths, to undo a miscount.
demoTitle: Make a !death command, then count with it.
demoReply: Ouch! Another one for the count.
listTitle: Choose what each value belongs to.
item1Desc: A channel counter holds one shared value. It suits a death count for the streamer or a total of wins during a challenge.
item2Desc: A viewer counter keeps separate values for each viewer. Create one on the Counters page, then use a configured command or reward to count for its caller.
item3Desc: A command counter separates values by command. The viewer-and-command scope separates them by both the viewer and the command.
item4Desc: Counters are created, set, reset, renamed and deleted on the Counters page. Use the scope that matches the total you want to keep.
limitsNote: A custom death counter changes when a configured command or reward bumps it, or when you edit it on the Counters page. Creating the counter does not detect deaths in a game.
prereq1: Connect ItsBagelBot to your Twitch channel and create a custom counter on the Counters page.
prereq2: Make a custom command with Bump a counter turned on, and pick your deaths counter.
faqQ1: How do I add a Twitch death counter?
faqA1: Create a channel counter named deaths on the Counters page. Then make a custom command such as !death, turn on its Bump a counter option and pick deaths. Each use adds 1.
faqQ2: Does the bot automatically detect deaths?
faqA2: A custom counter records updates you send to it. Bump it with a chat command, adjust it on the Counters page, or set up a channel-point reward to update it.
faqA3: Yes, when the command's permission allows everyone. Each use adds 1 for them. Only a moderator, lead moderator or the broadcaster can add a number to choose the step.
faqQ4: How do I reset the death count?
faqA4: Reset deaths on the Counters page. To correct the total instead, set it there to the replacement number, or have a moderator type !death -1 to remove one.
faqQ5: Can I keep a separate count for each viewer?
faqA5: Yes. Use the viewer scope when you create the counter. Channel scope shares one total; viewer scope keeps a separate value for each viewer. Command and viewer-and-command scopes are also supported.
ctaTitle: Set up the count before your next run.
